proxy.label: Current proxy
proxy.directVpnUnused: not used in Direct VPN mode
proxy.directVpnIdle: Direct VPN mode, tunnel not running
proxy.externalTunnel: not needed: another VPN/TUN is already running
proxy.notSelected: proxies found, but none is selected (listeners: {{count}})

routes.label: Default and TUN routes
routes.viaTun: Internet traffic goes through our TUN
routes.notViaTun: the TUN runs, but the route to the Internet bypasses it

endpoint.notRun: not checked: curl.exe did not run

tunLog.label: Engine log
tunLog.historical: TUN stopped, these are past entries (errors: {{count}}); they say nothing about the current route

appLog.label: App log
appLog.problems: warnings and errors in the last 15 minutes: {{count}}

routing.tunnelOff: Protection is off — there is no routing to check.
routing.inconclusive: Could not measure both IPs (some echo servers did not answer). Run the check again.
routing.leak: The SAME IP ({{vpn}}) is seen through the VPN and directly. The tunnel does not change your public address — this is a leak, or the proxy goes direct.
routing.smartUnverified: The tunnel works (VPN {{vpn}} ≠ direct {{direct}}), but the Smart-RU runtime check did not finish: no reliable Russian echo through the TUN. Routing rules are covered by config tests; this live self-test only confirms the general VPN/direct split.
routing.smartOk: Everything works as intended: foreign sites go through the VPN ({{vpn}}) and Russian sites go direct with your real IP ({{direct}}). Smart RU mode really splits the traffic.
routing.ruViaVpn: The tunnel works, but the Russian host went out through the VPN ({{ru}}) instead of directly ({{direct}}). The Russian domain lists may still be downloading — try again in a minute.
routing.ok: The tunnel works: {{vpn}} is seen through the VPN, {{direct}} directly. Your public address really changes.

plan.tunnelsUnverified: Could not check for other tunnels: a double tunnel is not ruled out.
plan.readyUnverified: All other start conditions are met, but the absence of a conflict is not confirmed.

doubleTunnel.title: Double tunnel found
doubleTunnel.explanation: This is exactly the setup that makes the Internet “sometimes die”: DNS and HTTPS can end up in a routing loop.
doubleTunnel.after: After: one active tunnel. Stop {{tun}}, or turn off TUN in the VPN client and keep only its proxy.
doubleTunnel.blocker: An external TUN and {{tun}} are active at the same time.
doubleTunnel.gate: Double tunnel found. This is exactly the setup that makes the Internet “sometimes die”: DNS and HTTPS can end up in a routing loop. After: one active tunnel. Stop {{tun}}, or turn off TUN in the VPN client and keep only its proxy.

foreignTun.title: A VPN/TUN is already on
foreignTun.explanation: Tunnel mode is not needed here and would do harm. The system already has an active tunnel, so the app must not add a second one.
foreignTun.after: After: the current VPN stays the main route; VPNTE only shows the status and helps set up apps when needed.
foreignTun.blocker: An external VPN/TUN is already active. Starting our protection would create a routing conflict.
foreignTun.gate: A VPN/TUN is already on. Tunnel mode is not needed here and would do harm. The system already has an active tunnel, so the app must not add a second one. After: the current VPN stays the main route; VPNTE only shows the status and helps set up apps when needed.

noProfile.title: No VPN profile selected
noProfile.explanation: Direct VPN mode needs no local proxy, but it needs an active server profile.
noProfile.before: Before: Direct VPN is on in the settings, but no server is selected.
noProfile.after: After: once a profile is selected, the app brings the TUN up straight to that VPN server.
noProfile.blocker: No active Direct VPN profile is selected.
noProfile.gate: No VPN profile selected. Direct VPN mode needs no local proxy, but it needs an active server profile. After: once a profile is selected, the app brings the TUN up straight to that VPN server.

directReady.title: Direct VPN can be turned on
directReady.explanation: Direct VPN mode needs no local proxy: only an active profile and no conflict with another TUN.
directReady.before: Before: the Internet takes the normal route, active profile {{profile}} is selected.
directReady.after: After: Internet traffic goes through {{tun}} straight to {{profile}}.

noProxy.title: Proxy not found
noProxy.explanation: Tunnel mode builds the system tunnel on top of a local proxy. Without a proxy the TUN must not start: traffic would go nowhere.
noProxy.after: After: once a proxy is on, the TUN gets a safe entry point.
noProxy.blocker: No local proxy found. There is nothing to turn into a system tunnel.
noProxy.gate: Proxy not found. Tunnel mode builds the system tunnel on top of a local proxy. Without a proxy the TUN must not start: traffic would go nowhere. After: once a proxy is on, the TUN gets a safe entry point.

proxyDead.title: Proxy does not answer
proxyDead.explanation: Starting the TUN on a closed proxy would break the Internet at once.
proxyDead.after: After: once the proxy runs, a safe route appears.
proxyDead.blocker: Proxy {{proxy}} was found but does not answer.
proxyDead.gate: Proxy does not answer. Starting the TUN on a closed proxy would break the Internet at once. After: once the proxy runs, a safe route appears.

hardReady.title: Tunnel mode can be turned on
hardReady.explanation: No conflicting TUN found and the proxy is alive. This is a safe setup for system-wide redirection.
hardReady.before: Before: the Internet takes the normal route, the proxy is available at {{proxy}}.
hardReady.after: After: Internet traffic goes through {{tun}}, and the proxy core is excluded from the tunnel so there is no loop.

removeDouble.label: Remove the double tunnel
removeDouble.before: Two system tunnels are on now: {{foreign}} and {{tun}}.
removeDouble.after: The app stops {{tun}}. One existing VPN/TUN remains, so DNS stops looping.

useExisting.label: Use the VPN that is already up
useExisting.after: VPNTE does not create a second TUN. This is safer: one route, no DNS loop.

viaProxy.label: Connect apps through the local proxy
viaProxy.after: In Proxy mode, apps that honour the Windows system proxy go through this proxy without a second TUN.

chooseProfile.label: Select a VPN profile
chooseProfile.before: Direct VPN has nowhere to connect: no active profile is selected.
chooseProfile.after: Once a profile is selected, the app can bring the TUN up straight to that server.

connectProfile.label: Connect the Direct VPN profile
connectProfile.before: There is no system {{tun}} now; active profile {{profile}} is ready to start.
connectProfile.after: VPNTE brings up one system tunnel straight to the selected VPN server.

lanDirectVpn.label: Keep the local network direct
lanDirectVpn.before: Local addresses and localhost must not go to the VPN server.
lanDirectVpn.after: The local network stays direct, Internet traffic goes through Direct VPN.

findProxy.label: Find a proxy
findProxy.before: There is no recognisable local proxy port now.
findProxy.after: Start your VPN client in Proxy mode; then the app can build the system TUN.

checkProxy.label: Check the proxy
checkProxy.before: {{proxy}} is selected, but the port does not accept connections.
checkProxy.after: Once the proxy answers, VPNTE can send all Internet traffic through it.

createTun.label: Create the system TUN
createTun.before: There is no system {{tun}} now, and proxy {{proxy}} works.
createTun.after: VPNTE creates one system tunnel and sends ordinary Internet traffic through this proxy.

lanDirectProxy.label: Keep the local network direct
lanDirectProxy.before: Local addresses and localhost must not go to the external proxy.
lanDirectProxy.after: The local network stays direct, Internet traffic goes through the proxy.

checkTunnels.label: Check for other tunnels
checkTunnels.before: Could not check for other tunnels: a double tunnel is not ruled out.
checkTunnels.after: Run the check again; it is not confirmed that there is no second TUN.
